title: A Serengeti Photography Tour for Your Club Comes Down to Three Choices: Season, Seats and Camp
meta_title: Serengeti Photography Tour Planning for Camera Clubs
meta_description: Planning a Serengeti photography tour for a club? Best months, 3-per-vehicle seating, bases, fees and drone rules, from our Nairobi team.
excerpt: A Serengeti photography tour for a group works best as a private 6-8 day trip timed to calving or the river crossings, with three photographers per vehicle. Here is how to plan seasons, seating, bases and fees.
content:
A Serengeti photography tour for a group works best as a private six- to eight-day trip timed to one stage of the migration, with three photographers per pop-up-roof vehicle. Clubs usually choose the calving herds at Ndutu from late January to March, or the Mara River crossings in the north from July to October.

If you organise a Serengeti photography tour for a camera club or a group of friends who all shoot seriously, the hard part is not finding animals. It is getting light, space and patience for everyone at once. This guide covers seasons, seating, bases, fees and the rules that catch groups out. Our club safaris for camera clubs and societies page shows how we set up private trips like this from Nairobi and Arusha.

Quick Facts

  • Best months: late January to March for calving at Ndutu; July to October for Mara River crossings in the north
  • Ideal length: 6-8 days, with at least three nights in one migration area
  • Seating: 3 photographers per vehicle (one window or hatch side each), 4 at most
  • Comfortable group size: 6-12 photographers in two to four vehicles
  • Park entry: US$82.60 per adult per 24 hours from 16 May to 14 March, US$70.80 from 15 March to 15 May (checked November 2026)
  • Light aircraft bags: 15 kg per soft-sided bag on Coastal Aviation scheduled flights (checked November 2026)
  • Drones: need a Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority permit and separate park permission before you travel

What Makes a Serengeti Photography Tour Different From a Normal Safari?

A Serengeti photography tour is planned around light and time at a sighting, not around ticking off species. Drives start before sunrise, the vehicle stays put when something is building, lunch is often packed so you never drive back to camp at noon, and the guide positions the car for the sun rather than for the closest view.

On a standard safari, a vehicle of six guests will usually move on after ten minutes at a sleeping lion. Photographers want the opposite: a cheetah on a termite mound may sit for an hour before it hunts. That patience only works when everyone in the car has signed up for it, which is why camera clubs book a private Serengeti photography tour.

The other difference is the vehicle. A 4x4 Land Cruiser with a pop-up roof is the norm on the northern circuit, and on a Serengeti photography tour the seating plan matters more than the model.

Who a Serengeti photography tour suits

Camera clubs, photography societies and friends travelling together all fit, as long as the group shares one rhythm. A beginner learns more beside a confident shooter than on a busy shared vehicle, so mixed-ability groups work well on a Serengeti photography tour.

When Should a Camera Club Book the Serengeti?

The best month for a Serengeti photography tour depends on the story your group wants to tell. Late January to March gives newborn calves and predator action; July to October gives river crossings in the north; June and November are quieter months with herds on the move.

The migration follows the rain, so dates for a Serengeti photography tour shift a little each year. Our great migration month-by-month guide shows where the herds usually are, and the table below turns that into what a photographer can expect.

MonthsWhere the herds usually areWhat photographers get
Late January to MarchNdutu and the southern short-grass plainsBirths, calves, cheetah and lion hunts, storm skies, clean green backgrounds
April to MayMoving north-west through the central plainsLong rains, dramatic clouds, few vehicles, some muddy tracks
JuneWestern corridor and central SerengetiLong columns of herds, rutting wildebeest, early dry-season light
July to OctoberNorthern Serengeti along the Mara RiverRiver crossings, crocodiles, dust and low sun behind the herds, more vehicles at crossing points
November to DecemberHeading south through the east and centreShort rains, fresh grass, resident cats around the Seronera kopjes

Calving season: the favourite for camera clubs

The calving months put hundreds of thousands of wildebeest on open plains where the grass is short and the horizon is clean. Most births fall in February. Predators follow the herds closely, so a group can photograph a newborn finding its feet in the morning and a cheetah chase in the afternoon. Our Serengeti calving season guide covers the timing in detail.

River crossings: drama with more company

Crossings on the Mara River are unpredictable. Herds can gather on a bank for hours and then turn away, and every vehicle nearby converges when they jump. A Serengeti photography tour built around crossings needs three or four nights in the north and patience with other vehicles.

Is a Serengeti photography tour worth it in the green season?

For groups that like moody skies, April and May can be the most rewarding Serengeti photography tour window of the year, and park entry drops to US$70.80 per adult from 15 March to 15 May. The catch is rain: afternoon storms can cut drives short and black-cotton soil turns slippery, so keep the itinerary flexible and choose camps that stay open.

How Many Photographers Should Share a Vehicle?

Three photographers per vehicle is the number we recommend for a serious group, so that each person has a full side of the car or a section of the open roof. Four still works with smaller lenses. Six, the usual safari seating, means people shoot over each other's shoulders and nobody gets the angle they came for.

That choice drives the budget of any Serengeti photography tour. The vehicle, fuel and driver-guide cost the same whether three or six people ride, so a group of twelve needs four vehicles at three per car instead of two at six. A sensible compromise is dedicated shooters three to a car and partners four or five to a car.

What to ask for in a photography vehicle

  • A pop-up roof that opens fully, not a small hatch
  • Bean bags or roof-mounted clamps, plus window rails you can rest a lens on
  • Charging points for camera batteries and laptops, and a cooler box for drinks
  • A driver-guide who knows how to read light and will switch off the engine for long exposures

Rooming, group size and the trip leader

A group of six to twelve fits most small camps. Single supplements add up quickly, so ask members early who is happy to share a twin. Name one leader for the Serengeti photography tour who collects preferences, gear questions and dietary needs before you book. Our page on how to organise a group safari has a step-by-step checklist for that role.

Where Should the Group Stay in the Serengeti?

The base should follow the herds. For calving, stay at or near Ndutu in the south. For June, the western corridor or central Serengeti. For crossings, the northern Serengeti around the Mara River. The central Serengeti around Seronera works year round for resident lions, leopards and cheetahs on the kopjes.

Each move between areas costs half a day of shooting, so a Serengeti photography tour works best with fewer bases and longer stays. Three nights in one place give you time to learn where a cheetah family hunts.

Ndutu lies inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area rather than the national park, so you pay the conservation area fee there. Seasonal mobile camps follow the herds south for calving and north for the crossings, while permanent lodges suit the centre. Our best Serengeti camps by area post explains which zones suit which months.

A sample eight-day route for a camera club

Our 8 Day Tanzania Calving Season Photo Safari gives a good shape for a club in February: Tarangire for elephants and baobabs, three nights on the Ndutu plains, time in the central Serengeti, and a full day on the Ngorongoro Crater floor. For July to October, the 8 Day Great Migration Northern Tanzania trip can be adapted with extra nights in the north and photography seating.

How Much Does a Serengeti Photography Tour Cost for a Group?

A Serengeti photography tour costs more per person than a standard safari, because fewer people share each vehicle and migration camps charge high-season rates. As a rough estimate, allow US$450-900 per person per day mid-range and US$900-1,600 or more at higher-end camps, sharing.

Government fees set the floor and are the same for everyone. The table below shows the main ones a group will pay; see our Tanzania park fees guide for the full list, and always confirm current rates with Tanzania National Parks (TANAPA) before you set a club price.

Cost itemAmount (checked November 2026)How it works for a group
Serengeti entryUS$82.60 per adult per 24 hours (US$70.80 from 15 March to 15 May)Per person, per 24-hour period from entry time
Concession feeUS$70.80 per adult per night July to September, US$59 October to JuneOnly when you sleep in a camp or lodge inside the park; often built into the room rate
Ngorongoro Conservation AreaUS$70.80 per adult per 24 hoursApplies at Ndutu and on the main road from Arusha
Crater service feeUS$295 per vehicle per descentSplit between the people in each vehicle, so it costs more per head at three per car
Vehicle, fuel and driver-guidePriced per vehicle per dayThe main reason a three-per-car trip costs more than a six-per-car one

Two points help organisers price a Serengeti photography tour. Decide the seating plan before you ask for a quote, because a price built on six per car will look cheap and then rise. Then publish a club price that already includes every park, concession and crater fee. Our Serengeti safari cost breakdown explains the per-day bands in more depth.

Gear, Flights, Drones and Park Rules for Photographers

The rules that trip up photography groups are luggage limits on light aircraft, drone permits and behaviour at sightings. Sort all three before departure, and brief every member in writing, so nobody arrives at an airstrip with a hard case or a drone that cannot leave the bag.

Luggage on light aircraft

Coastal Aviation, which flies scheduled routes to Serengeti airstrips, allows 15 kg per checked bag, and bags must be soft-sided (checked November 2026). The airline asks passengers to discuss photography equipment with its reservations team at booking, and an extra freight seat can be bought in advance for heavy kit. Anyone on a Serengeti photography tour carrying a 600mm lens and two bodies often books that seat, or travels by road.

Flying a drone

The Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority says every drone flight in Tanzania needs its approval and a permit, including recreational use, and foreign visitors should apply three to four weeks before arrival (checked November 2026). Flying in a national park needs a separate permission from the park authority as well. In practice, most groups on a Serengeti photography tour leave drones at home.

Behaviour at crossings and sightings

Stay seated inside the vehicle, never ask a guide to block a crossing point, and keep voices down near cats. In 2025 the parks authority suspended several guides after vehicles blocked a Mara River crossing and guests left their vehicles or sat on bonnets. A good guide on a Serengeti photography tour gets the angle by reading the herd and arriving early, not by pushing in.

Insider Tips

  • Seating: rotate seats daily so everyone gets the best side of the car
  • Lenses: a 100-400mm or 150-600mm zoom covers most Serengeti sightings; add a wide lens for skies and herds
  • Dust: pack rocket blowers, lens cloths and pillowcases to cover cameras between sightings in the dry months
  • Back-ups: bring two cards per day of shooting and a laptop or portable drive for nightly back-ups
  • Timings: agree in advance that drives leave before sunrise, with breakfast packed for the vehicle
  • Non-shooters: give partners their own vehicle or a camp morning, so the photographers can wait at a sighting

Why a Private Group Beats Joining a Scheduled Photo Tour

A private Serengeti photography tour lets your club set the pace, the seating and the subjects, rather than fitting around strangers with different goals. You choose dates around members' calendars and pay one clear price per person.

On a mixed departure, one guest's wish to see a leopard can pull the car away from a cheetah about to hunt. With your own vehicles, the group decides together and radios share every sighting. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best month for a Serengeti photography tour?

The best month for a Serengeti photography tour is February for most groups, when calving peaks on the Ndutu plains and predators hunt in the open. July to October suits groups who want Mara River crossings in the north. April and May bring dramatic skies and fewer vehicles, but rain can shorten some drives.

How many people should share a vehicle on a photography safari?

Three photographers per vehicle is ideal on a Serengeti photography safari, giving each person a side of the car or part of the roof. Four still works with smaller lenses. The standard six per vehicle is fine for general safaris, but photographers end up shooting around each other and missing the best angles.

Can I fly a drone in the Serengeti?

Flying a drone in the Serengeti is not something to plan casually. The Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority requires a permit for every drone flight, including recreational ones, and asks foreign visitors to apply three to four weeks ahead. A national park also needs its own separate permission, so most photography groups leave drones at home.

How much camera gear can I take on a light aircraft to the Serengeti?

Scheduled light aircraft to the Serengeti, such as Coastal Aviation, allow 15 kg per checked bag, and bags must be soft-sided. Photographers with heavy lenses can buy an extra freight seat in advance or travel by road instead. Always declare photography equipment when you book, as the airline asks.

How long should a group photography trip to the Serengeti be?

A group photography trip to the Serengeti should last six to eight days, with at least three nights in one migration area. Fewer, longer stays mean more time at sightings and less time on the road. Adding Tarangire and the Ngorongoro Crater rounds out an eight-day northern Tanzania route nicely.

Final Thoughts

A Serengeti photography tour pays off when the group agrees on one season, three photographers per car and long stays in fewer bases. Get those three decisions right and the herds and the light do the rest.
